key_insight: A fully discrete scheme couples porous flow, viscoelastic deformation and frictional fracture contact, with proven discrete existence, uniqueness, stability and a priori error estimates.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports numerical simulation of fractured porous materials where fluid flow, deformation and fracture-surface friction interact.
method: Represent fractures as codimension-one interfaces coupled to Darcy flow in the matrix and fractures.
Combine linear viscoelasticity with normal compliance and Coulomb friction at fracture surfaces.
Discretize using conforming finite elements in space and implicit Euler time stepping.
evidence_signal: A numerical experiment computes numerical errors and compares them with the theoretical error estimates.
watch_item: The abstract reports only one numerical experiment, leaving robustness across broader geometries and loading conditions unestablished.
paper_title: Numerical analysis of coupled flow, deformation and frictional contact mechanics in a fractured porous medium
